name: Great Barrier Reef
hook: The largest living structure on Earth, off Queensland — and the only one you can see from orbit.

facts.label: the largest coral reef system
facts.statement: Stretching some 1,400 miles off Australia's northeast coast, it is the world's largest coral reef system, built by hundreds of coral species.

facts.label: Queensland
facts.statement: It lies off Queensland, the "royal" state named for Queen Victoria whose territory includes part of the reef.

facts.label: the Coral Sea
facts.statement: The reef gave its name to the Coral Sea, which lies off Queensland between Australia and Papua New Guinea.

facts.label: Captain James Cook
facts.statement: In 1770 Captain Cook's Endeavour ran aground on the reef and nearly sank, after he had charted New Zealand.

facts.label: coral bleaching
facts.statement: In 2018 National Geographic reported half the reef dead, "akin to a forest after a devastating fire"; crown-of-thorns starfish also eat the coral.

facts.label: Steve Irwin
facts.statement: Steve Irwin, television's Crocodile Hunter and an Australian folk hero, died in 2006 when a stingray's barb struck him at the reef.

facts.label: a World Heritage Site
facts.statement: It is a UNESCO World Heritage Site, and removing coral can bring a fine of up to $53,000.
